newsitem.title: USA: Clinton names Arkansas friend Veterans' Secretary.
newsitem.headline: Clinton names Arkansas friend Veterans' Secretary.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Thursday he would nominate deputy Secretary of Veterans' Affairs Hershel Gober to head the department, replacing Jesse Brown who resigned on Tuesday.

"I intend to nominate deputy Secretary Gober to be the next Secretary of Veterans' Affairs," Clinton said at a White House ceremony at which veterans' organisations pledged their support for the expansion of NATO.

Gober, a two-tour veteran of the Vietnam War whose 20-year military career included service in both the army and marines, was director of the Arkansas Department of Veterans' Affairs when Clinton was state governor. His military decorations include the Purple Heart, Bronze Star and Soldier's Medal.

As the number two man at the federal agency for veterans, he has actively pressed for expansion of benefits to Vietnam veterans exposed to the defoliant Agent Orange and Gulf War veterans who suffer from undiagnosed illness.
If confirmed by the Senate, Gober will be responsible for maintaining a nationwide network of resources and services for the 26 million U.S. military veterans.
Brown, who has held the job for the last five years, resigned to return to private life.

The Veterans' Department is made up of three organisations that administer programmes to benefit veterans and their families -- the Veterans Health Administration, the Veteran Benefits Administration and the National Cemetery System.
It employs 235,000 people around the country.
